I've started three read-only reviewers on `b64ff41..5d17656`, which covers the last three commits on main (56d4bde, 487da95, 5d17656):

- **Reviewer A:** Opus
- **Reviewer B:** Sonnet

Each one is told to report only real bugs, no nits, and not to touch any files. They're focused on:

- leftover references to the deleted orchestrate, autopilot and multi-phase-plan playbooks and their scripts

When all three report back, I'll merge their findings and give you the verdict. Nothing in the repo will be changed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Links shipit's skills into ~/.claude/skills and its agents into ~/.claude/agents.
# Symlinks, so edits in this repo apply to the next session. Safe to rerun.
#   ./install.sh            install or refresh
#   ./install.sh --dry-run  show what it would do
#   ./install.sh --uninstall  remove only links that point into this repo
set -euo pipefail

repo="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
claude="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
mode="install"
case "${1:-}" in
  --dry-run) mode="dry" ;;
  --uninstall) mode="uninstall" ;;
  "") ;;
  *) echo "usage: $0 [--dry-run|--uninstall]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

run() { if [ "$mode" = dry ]; then echo "would: $*"; else "$@"; fi; }

link() {
  local src="$1" dst="$2"
  if [ "$mode" = uninstall ]; then
    if [ -L "$dst" ] && [[ "$(readlink "$dst")" == "$repo"/* ]]; then
      rm "$dst" && echo "removed $dst"
    fi
    return
  fi
  if [ -L "$dst" ]; then
    [ "$(readlink "$dst")" = "$src" ] && return
    [[ "$(readlink "$dst")" == "$repo"/* ]] || { echo "skip $dst: links somewhere else ($(readlink "$dst"))" >&2; return; }
    run rm "$dst"
  elif [ -e "$dst" ]; then
    echo "skip $dst: a real file or folder is there, not touching it" >&2
    return
  fi
  run ln -s "$src" "$dst"
  [ "$mode" = dry ] || echo "linked $dst"
}

run mkdir -p "$claude/skills" "$claude/agents" "$claude/shipit"

for dir in "$repo"/skills/*/; do
  name="$(basename "$dir")"
  link "${dir%/}" "$claude/skills/$name"
done
for file in "$repo"/agents/*.md; do

done

if [ "$mode" = install ]; then
  echo
  echo "shipit is installed. In a new Claude Code session:"
  echo "  /setup-shipit   pick models per role (optional; defaults work)"
  echo "  /shipit <task>  route a task to a playbook"
fi

The three commits (56d4bde, 487da95, 5d17656) have five real bugs, all in the three new scripts. Nothing was changed in the repo, but one reviewer accidentally left a stray cache file in it (see the last section). I ran two checks of my own to confirm the most important claims.

### Intent
> These commits do three things. They switch the reading roles to Haiku at the budget's starting effort, based on a recorded eval. They add a trivial lane to /shipit, an opt-in hook that refuses PRs with no Proof section (`require-proof.py`) and a cost script (`cost.py`), and they delete the fleet playbooks and their scripts, leaving 22 routed playbooks. They also let /setup-shipit trust chosen GitHub owners in auto mode by rewriting `autoMode.environment` in `settings.json`, with a backup (`automode_repos.py`).

### Reviewers
All three ran at high effort, one step below the default, to stay inside the $8 budget.
- **Reviewer A:** Opus, 8 findings
- **Reviewer B:** Sonnet, 9 findings
- **Reviewer C:** Fable, 7 findings

### Act On
1. **The proof hook checks the whole shell command instead of the PR body** (A, C; I reproduced it). It treats whatever follows `## Proof` as that section's content. When Proof is the last section, that is just the closing `"`, a heredoc's `EOF`, or the next flag. So `gh pr create --title x --body "## Why\nA\n\n## Proof\n"` exits 0. A `## Proof` inside `--title`, or in an `echo` earlier in the same command, also passes. The reverse fails too: `--body "$(cat pr.md)"` is blocked even when the file has a Proof section. The existing test only covers an empty Proof section followed by another heading, which is why it passes. `require-proof.py:36-49`
2. **The proof hook lets the PR through when it can't read the body file** (A, B, C). Then `body_of` returns `None` and the hook exits 0. That covers `--body-file -` / `-F -`, a missing file, and a relative path after a `cd`. It also covers the usual agent pattern of writing the body file and running `gh pr create` in one Bash call: the hook runs before the command, so the file doesn't exist yet. Two related misses (A): `gh -R o/r pr create` and `gh pr new`. In the other direction, any command that just mentions the phrase is blocked, such as `git commit -m "…gh pr create…"` or `grep "gh pr create"` (A, B). This repo's docs mention it often. `require-proof.py:23-35, 60, 66`
3. **The setup script can replace auto mode's built-in rules instead of adding to them.** This is two bugs in the same function, which I confirmed by reading `automode_repos.py:87-102`:
   - With no `autoMode` section, `setdefault` creates an `environment` list with only the five new lines and no `"$defaults"` (A, B). Your own `auto-mode.md:29` says to keep `"$defaults"`, so this would likely drop auto mode's other default lines (Host containment, Secrets management and so on).
   - When `"$defaults"` is present, which is the setup the repo recommends, none of the labels match, so all five lines are appended (C). The built-in "Source control: …no additional orgs configured" line stays and contradicts the new "Trusted owners" line. The dry run only shows `+` lines, so you never see the conflict.
4. **The settings rewrite loosens file permissions and breaks symlinks** (permissions: A, B; symlink: A, B, C). The temp file is created with your default permissions, so a `0600` `settings.json` becomes `0664` or `0644`. A group-writable `settings.json` lets others in that group add hook commands that run on every tool call. If `settings.json` is a symlink from a dotfiles repo, `os.replace` swaps it for a plain file. `automode_repos.py:113-118`
5. **`cost.py` undercounts the bill.** There are two causes:
   - Every cache write is priced at the 5-minute rate (A, B). The local transcripts both reviewers checked are all 1-hour writes, which cost 2× input.
   - `family()` matches on substring, so older models get the newest model's price (A, B, C). For example, Haiku 4.5 is priced 10× too low and `claude-fable-5` cache reads 4× too low.
   
   Reviewer A re-priced 123 local transcripts: the script said $923 against a corrected $1,222, about 24% low. `cost.py:19-33, 72-80`

### Consider
- **Users who already ran setup stay on Sonnet** (A only, not verified). If the old /setup-shipit wrote `how explorer: sonnet` lines into `models.md`, those override the new default. A re-run keeps them because they now differ from it.
- **Budgets below `large` run Haiku at `high`** (B). That is the setting the eval scored worst, below the old Sonnet default.
- **The remote scan misses common GitHub URL forms** (A, C). It misses `ssh://`, SSH host aliases like `github.com-work`, and `https://user@`. It also skips worktrees, where `.git` is a file. Those owners are never offered as choices.
- **`maintain-verification-skill` now reads `source readers`** instead of `verification` (A, B), so an existing `verification:` override silently stops applying.
- **`cost.py` hardcodes `~/.claude`** (B). `install.sh` honours `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so the cost receipt fails for anyone who sets it.

### Noted
- `shipit/SKILL.md` says Haiku costs "about a fifteenth" of Sonnet. The eval doc's own caveat puts the worst case at about 3×, since Haiku is billed 5× over 100K-token prompts (B; C thought the figure checked out but missed the caveat).
- Existing lines are only matched in the bold `**Label**:` form (B).
- Fast-mode pricing is ignored (A, not seen in your transcripts).
- A non-list `environment` raises `TypeError`, and a missing `settings.json` raises `FileNotFoundError` (C).
- A Proof section whose first line starts with `#`, such as `#123 fixed`, is rejected (B).

### Dismissed
Nothing. The reviewers stayed on real bugs. All three checked these and found them clean:
- No references to the deleted playbooks or scripts remain.
- The router lists 22 playbooks and there are 22 files.
- `package.json` was updated.
- The hook follows the hooks contract (exit 2 plus stderr), and its test runs and passes.
- `cost.py` correctly de-duplicates repeated message lines and finds subagent transcripts.
